description: Landing and onboarding site for a contract review API that lets developers integrate AI-powered legal clause analysis into their apps — marketing pages plus a multi-step integration wizard

pages.name: home
pages.description: Marketing landing page introducing the contract review API to engineering teams at law-adjacent companies
components: Top navigation with wordmark, primary links (Product, Docs, Pricing, Customers, Changelog), a 'Sign in' text link, and a 'Get API key' primary button

Hero with eyebrow label, headline, supporting paragraph, two buttons ('Start integrating' primary, 'Read the docs' secondary), and a code-sample panel showing a POST /v1/contracts/review request with a language tab switcher and copy button
Logo strip labelled 'Trusted by legal and ops teams at' with six grayscale company marks
Three-column feature row — each column has an icon, feature name (Clause extraction, Risk scoring, Redline suggestions), one-paragraph description, and a 'Learn more' link
Footer with four link columns (Product, Developers, Company, Legal), a status indicator pill showing 'All systems operational', and a copyright line

pages.name: wizard
pages.description: Five-step integration wizard that walks a developer from account creation to a first successful API call
components: Wizard top bar with wordmark, a horizontal five-step indicator (Create workspace, Verify org, Choose plan, Generate keys, Make first call) with current step highlighted, and a 'Save & exit' link

Step content panel on the left half — for the active step shows step title, helper paragraph, and the relevant form (workspace name input, region dropdown, team-size radio group) with inline validation hints

Right-side context panel that updates per step — currently shows a 'What happens next' card listing three bullet points, a 'Need a paralegal review' callout linking to human-in-the-loop add-on, and a small FAQ accordion with three questions
Sticky footer action bar with a 'Back' secondary button on the left, a step counter ('Step 1 of 5') centered, and a 'Continue' primary button on the right

pages.name: wizard-keys
pages.description: Penultimate wizard step where the developer generates API credentials and tests a sandbox call
components: Same wizard top bar with step 4 of 5 active

Credentials panel showing two generated keys (Publishable key, Secret key) each in a monospaced read-only field with a reveal toggle, a copy button, and a 'Rotate' link, plus a warning callout that the secret key will only be shown once
Scope selector below the keys — a checklist of permission scopes (contracts:read, contracts:write, clauses:extract, redlines:suggest, webhooks:manage) each with a short description

Live sandbox tester panel — request builder with method locked to POST, endpoint field, JSON body editor pre-filled with a sample NDA payload, a 'Send test request' button, and a response viewer with status, latency, and JSON tree
Footer action bar with Back, step counter, and a 'Continue to first call' primary button that is disabled until a successful sandbox response is received

pages.name: pricing
pages.description: Pricing page comparing self-serve plans and an enterprise tier with a usage estimator
components: Top navigation (same as home)
Page heading 'Pricing built around contracts reviewed' with a billing-period toggle (Monthly / Annual) and a region selector
Three plan cards in a row — Developer, Team, Scale — each card lists price, included monthly contract count, a feature checklist, and a 'Choose plan' button; the Team card has a 'Most popular' ribbon

Usage estimator panel — a slider for monthly contracts reviewed, a slider for average pages per contract, a dropdown for jurisdictions covered, and an output area showing estimated monthly cost broken into base plus overage line items
Enterprise band at the bottom with headline, paragraph about SSO, audit logs, BAA and dedicated legal-ops support, a 'Talk to sales' button, and three logos of representative enterprise customers

pages.name: docs
pages.description: Documentation reading view for a single API reference page
components: Docs top bar with wordmark, a docs-scoped search input with keyboard shortcut hint, version selector dropdown (v1, v2 beta), and a 'Dashboard' link
Left sidebar with collapsible navigation tree grouped by section (Getting started, Authentication, Contracts, Clauses, Redlines, Webhooks, Errors) with the current page highlighted

Center reading column with breadcrumb, page title 'Review a contract', endpoint signature block (HTTP verb pill + path), parameters table (name, type, required, description), and a response schema table
Right-rail in-page table of contents listing the headings on the current page with the active section highlighted, plus a 'Was this page helpful?' thumbs up/down widget at the bottom
Sticky right-side code panel showing request and response examples in tabs (curl, Node, Python) with a 'Run in playground' link that opens the sandbox

pages.name: customers
pages.description: Customer stories index page showcasing how legal-tech and ops teams use the API
components: Top navigation (same as home)
Page header with title 'How teams ship contract workflows faster', a one-line summary, and a filter chip row (All, Legal tech, Fintech, Real estate, HR platforms)
Featured case study banner — large quote, attributed name and role, company logo, three KPI tiles (contracts processed monthly, review time reduction, error rate), and a 'Read the full story' link
Grid of customer story cards (three per row) — each card has company logo, industry tag, one-sentence outcome, and a 'Read story' link
Closing call-to-action band with headline 'Start reviewing contracts in an afternoon', a 'Get API key' primary button, and a 'Book a demo' secondary button
